it-alto-adige-aldein-aich.name: Aldein-Aich
it-alto-adige-aldein-aich.summary: Aldein-Aich lies on the high Aldein plateau, among the highest UGAs, giving taut Pinot Bianco and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-aldein-aich.terroir: Porphyry soils with cool nights at altitude. The official boundary, in Aldino/Aldein, reaches from about 520 to 1080 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-aldein-aich.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-aldein-aich.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-altenburg.name: Altenburg
it-alto-adige-altenburg.summary: Altenburg is a small, high hamlet above Kaltern near the Rastenbach gorge and an early Christian church site, giving Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-altenburg.terroir: Limestone and dolomite debris at altitude. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 600 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-altenburg.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-altenburg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-barleit.name: Barleit
it-alto-adige-barleit.grapes: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Gewürztraminer, Schiava, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-barleit.summary: Barleit lies below Kaltern towards the lake, giving Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Gewürztraminer, Schiava and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-barleit.terroir: Moraine and gravel. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 260 to 410 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Gewürztraminer, Schiava, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-barleit.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-barleit.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-brenntal.name: Brenntal
it-alto-adige-brenntal.summary: Brenntal ('burnt valley') is the hottest site of Kurtatsch, a south-facing bowl at the foot of the village where Kellerei Kurtatsch grows its top Merlot and Cabernet and a rich Gewürztraminer. Its name says it all: the gravel and the rock walls radiate heat late into the evening.
it-alto-adige-brenntal.terroir: Calcareous gravel and debris at about 220 to 300 m. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch and Termeno/Tramin, lies at about 400 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Gewürztraminer, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-brenntal.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-brenntal.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-brixner.name: Brixner
it-alto-adige-brixner.summary: Brixner covers the vineyards around Brixen and Vahrn, the northernmost wine area of Italy, including those of the Augustinian abbey of Neustift (Novacella). Sylvaner, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling and Kerner are allowed, and they give crisp, aromatic, mineral whites.
it-alto-adige-brixner.terroir: Quartz phyllite, granite debris and moraine on steep south-facing terraces at roughly 550 to 900 m. The official boundary, in Bressanone/Brixen and Varna/Vahrn, reaches from about 560 to 900 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Sylvaner, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, Kerner.
it-alto-adige-brixner.nerd_note: The Eisacktal is Alto Adige's white-wine valley, with steep terraces up to about 900 m and soils of quartz phyllite, granite and moraine; Cantina Valle Isarco in Klausen and the abbey of Neustift are its anchors.
it-alto-adige-brixner.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-buchholz.name: Buchholz
it-alto-adige-buchholz.summary: Buchholz is a mountain hamlet above Salurn, where vineyards climb to about 900 m. Haderburg, a pioneer of Alto Adige sparkling wine, grows Chardonnay and Pinot Nero here for its classic-method wines.
it-alto-adige-buchholz.terroir: Porphyry and calcareous soils on steep, high slopes. The official boundary, in Salorno/Salurn, reaches from about 210 to 920 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-buchholz.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-buchholz.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-colli-di-bolzano.name: Colli di Bolzano
it-alto-adige-colli-di-bolzano.summary: Schiava from the slopes around Bolzano outside the St. Magdalener zone, slightly lighter in style.
it-alto-adige-colli-di-bolzano.terroir: Porphyry and moraine around the Bolzano basin.

it-alto-adige-dorf.name: Dorf
it-alto-adige-dorf.summary: Dorf is the area around the village of Kaltern itself, giving Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-dorf.terroir: Morainic and calcareous soils on gentle slopes. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 300 to 540 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-dorf.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-dorf.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-eggen.name: Eggen
it-alto-adige-eggen.summary: Eggen lies on the lower slopes of Kurtatsch, giving Chardonnay, Schiava and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-eggen.terroir: Moraine and calcareous debris. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, lies at about 350 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Schiava, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-eggen.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-eggen.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-entiklar.name: Entiklar
it-alto-adige-entiklar.summary: Entiklar is the hamlet below Kurtatsch where the Tiefenbrunner family's Turmhof castle-winery stands. Its UGA allows Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-entiklar.terroir: Calcareous gravel at the foot of the slope. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, reaches from about 210 to 540 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-entiklar.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-entiklar.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.name: Eppan Berg
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.summary: Eppan Berg (Monte di Appiano) is the higher, cooler hillside above Eppan towards the Mendola range, and one of Alto Adige's best sources of Pinot Bianco and Pinot Nero. Stroblhof's Pinot Nero and many cooperative top whites come from here.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.terroir: Limestone and dolomite debris over porphyry, the vineyards climbing towards the Mendel cliffs. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, reaches from about 390 to 710 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-eppan-berg-schulthaus.name: Eppan Berg-Schulthaus
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg-schulthaus.summary: Schulthaus is a single-variety UGA on Eppan Berg reserved for Pinot Bianco, and the source of Cantina San Michele Appiano's Pinot Bianco Schulthauser, one of the best-known whites of the region.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg-schulthaus.terroir: Calcareous debris over porphyry on the high slopes of Eppan Berg. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, reaches from about 470 to 680 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg-schulthaus.nerd_note: It is one of only a handful of UGAs restricted to a single grape.
it-alto-adige-eppan-berg-schulthaus.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-feld.name: Feld
it-alto-adige-feld.grapes: Moscato Giallo, Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet
it-alto-adige-feld.summary: Feld lies on the flat, warm ground south of the Kalterer See towards Pfatten, giving Moscato Giallo, Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-feld.terroir: Lake sediments and gravel on the valley floor. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern and Vadena/Pfatten, reaches from about 220 to 470 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Moscato Giallo, Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-feld.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-feld.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-frag.name: Frag
it-alto-adige-frag.summary: Frag lies between Villanders and Klausen on the west side of the Eisacktal, a UGA reserved for Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-frag.terroir: Quartz phyllite and moraine. The official boundary, in Villandro/Villanders and Chiusa/Klausen, reaches from about 580 to 940 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-frag.nerd_note: The Eisacktal is Alto Adige's white-wine valley, with steep terraces up to about 900 m and soils of quartz phyllite, granite and moraine; Cantina Valle Isarco in Klausen and the abbey of Neustift are its anchors.
it-alto-adige-frag.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-frauenrigl.name: Frauenrigl
it-alto-adige-frauenrigl.summary: Frauenrigl is a warm, low Kurtatsch site for Gewürztraminer, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-frauenrigl.terroir: Calcareous gravel. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, lies at about 240 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Gewürztraminer, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-frauenrigl.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-frauenrigl.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-freiberg.name: Freiberg
it-alto-adige-freiberg.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-freiberg.summary: Freiberg lies high on the slopes above Meran near the castle of the same name, a cool site for Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-freiberg.terroir: Gneiss and moraine at altitude. The official boundary, in Merano/Meran, reaches from about 280 to 770 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-freiberg.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-freiberg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-furggl.name: Furggl
it-alto-adige-furggl.summary: Furggl lies at Auer on the valley floor below the Castelfeder hill, giving Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio and Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-furggl.terroir: Gravel and porphyry debris. The official boundary, in Ora/Auer, reaches from about 220 to 300 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-furggl.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-furggl.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-giatl.name: Giatl
it-alto-adige-giatl.summary: Giatl lies in Kurtinig, the smallest wine village of the Bassa Atesina (Unterland), on the flat valley floor of the Adige, giving Chardonnay and Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-giatl.terroir: Alluvial sand and gravel at around 210 m, among the lowest UGAs. The official boundary, in Cortina/Kurtinig and Magrè/Margreid, lies at about 210 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio.
it-alto-adige-giatl.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-giatl.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-girlan.name: Girlan
it-alto-adige-girlan.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Schiava, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-girlan.summary: Girlan (Cornaiano) is a village on the Überetsch plateau west of Bolzano, home of the cooperative Cantina Girlan and of Colterenzio (Schreckbichl). Its UGA allows Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Schiava and Pinot Nero, and the village is known for elegant, cool-climate Pinot Nero and old-vine Schiava.
it-alto-adige-girlan.terroir: Morainic gravel and limestone debris on the plateau, open to the Ora wind from Lake Garda in the afternoon. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, reaches from about 300 to 510 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Schiava, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-girlan.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-girlan.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-girlan-gschleier.name: Girlan-Gschleier
it-alto-adige-girlan-gschleier.summary: Gschleier is a small, high part of Girlan reserved for Schiava alone. Cantina Girlan's Gschleier, from vines often more than a century old on traditional pergolas, showed that Schiava can be a serious, age-worthy wine.
it-alto-adige-girlan-gschleier.terroir: Morainic soils on the plateau edge. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, lies at about 430 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava.
it-alto-adige-girlan-gschleier.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-girlan-gschleier.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-glen.name: Glen
it-alto-adige-glen.summary: Glen is a hamlet above Montan, reserved for Pinot Nero, which gives fine, cool-climate wines on these west-facing slopes.
it-alto-adige-glen.terroir: Porphyry and calcareous soils. The official boundary, in Montagna/Montan, reaches from about 410 to 800 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-glen.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-glen.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-graun.name: Graun
it-alto-adige-graun.summary: Graun is the highest wine hamlet of Kurtatsch, with vines reaching beyond 900 m, reserved for Müller-Thurgau. Kellerei Kurtatsch's Müller-Thurgau Graun is a crisp, floral mountain wine.
it-alto-adige-graun.terroir: Calcareous and dolomitic soils on a high terrace. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, reaches from about 400 to 1050 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Müller-Thurgau.
it-alto-adige-graun.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.
it-alto-adige-graun.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-gries.name: Gries
it-alto-adige-gries.summary: Gries is the old garden suburb of Bolzano on the alluvial fan of the Talfer river, and the historic home of Lagrein. The deep, warm gravel and sand soils, sheltered by the Guncina hill and baked by the hottest summers of the region, give dark, velvety Lagrein with violet and cocoa notes. The Benedictines of Muri-Gries have made wine here since the nineteenth century, and Cantina Bolzano's Lagrein Riserva Taber is a benchmark.
it-alto-adige-gries.terroir: Alluvial gravel and sand of the Talfer delta on the flat valley floor; Bolzano's basin traps heat, so this is one of Italy's warmest red-wine sites north of the Alps. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 240 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-gries.nerd_note: 'Lagrein Gries' was a recognised traditional name long before the UGA system; the 2024 UGA turns it into a defined site.
it-alto-adige-gries.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-gries-moritzing.name: Gries-Moritzing
it-alto-adige-gries-moritzing.summary: Gries-Moritzing is the western, sunniest part of the Gries fan towards the hamlet of Moritzing, reserved for Lagrein alone. The wines are deep coloured, juicy and firm, the essence of Bolzano's own red grape.
it-alto-adige-gries-moritzing.terroir: Alluvial gravel and sand at the foot of the porphyry slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 240 to 410 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-gries-moritzing.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-gries-moritzing.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-griesfeld.name: Griesfeld
it-alto-adige-griesfeld.summary: Griesfeld lies on the valley floor at Neumarkt, a UGA reserved for Lagrein, which thrives on the warm, deep gravel soils.
it-alto-adige-griesfeld.terroir: Alluvial gravel and sand. The official boundary, in Egna/Neumarkt, lies at about 240 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Lagrein.
it-alto-adige-griesfeld.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-griesfeld.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-huberfeld.name: Huberfeld
it-alto-adige-huberfeld.summary: Huberfeld lies on the warmer lower ground of Eppan, where Chardonnay, Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet ripen fully.
it-alto-adige-huberfeld.terroir: Gravel and moraine. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, lies at about 270 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-huberfeld.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-huberfeld.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-kalditsch.name: Kalditsch
it-alto-adige-kalditsch.summary: Kalditsch is a high Montan site at around 650 m, reserved for Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-kalditsch.terroir: Porphyry soils at altitude. The official boundary, in Montagna/Montan, lies at about 660 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-kalditsch.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-kalditsch.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-kampenn.name: Kampenn
it-alto-adige-kampenn.summary: Kampenn sits on the hillside south-east of Bolzano below Kohlern, a cooler, higher site where Chardonnay, Kerner and Sauvignon join Schiava.
it-alto-adige-kampenn.terroir: Porphyry and moraine on east and south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, lies at about 590 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Kerner, Sauvignon Blanc, Schiava.
it-alto-adige-kampenn.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.

it-alto-adige-margreid-leiten.summary: Margreid-Leiten covers the slopes above Margreid, the village of Alois Lageder, giving Chardonnay, Gewürztraminer, Schiava, Merlot and Cabernet.

it-alto-adige-mazon.name: Mazon
it-alto-adige-mazon.summary: Mazon (Mazzon) is a terrace above Neumarkt and the most celebrated Pinot Nero site of Italy. Its west-facing slope catches afternoon sun while the Ora wind from Lake Garda cools it; clay and limestone over porphyry give finely structured, perfumed Pinot. Hofstätter's Barthenau Vigna Sant'Urbano, Gottardi and Brunnenhof are references, and Mazon is reserved for Pinot Nero alone.
it-alto-adige-mazon.terroir: Clay-rich calcareous soils over porphyry on a gently sloping terrace facing west across the Adige valley. The official boundary, in Egna/Neumarkt, reaches from about 220 to 780 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-mazon.nerd_note: Pinot Nero was planted here in the nineteenth century under the Habsburgs, when Ludwig Barth von Barthenau brought Burgundian vines to his estate.

it-alto-adige-meranese.name: Meranese
it-alto-adige-meranese.summary: Light Schiava from the hills around Merano, the old Habsburg spa town, including the Burgraviato area. Fresh, fruity and meant for drinking young.
it-alto-adige-meranese.terroir: Moraine and gneiss slopes of the Merano basin.
it-alto-adige-meranese.nerd_note: Meranese is also called Meraner Hügel (Merano hill) on older labels.

it-alto-adige-mezzan.name: Mezzan
it-alto-adige-mezzan.summary: Mezzan is a Kaltern site reserved for Pinot Nero, one of the few single-variety UGAs.

it-alto-adige-milla.summary: Milla is a Kurtatsch site on the warm lower slopes, giving Chardonnay, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-milla.terroir: Calcareous debris. The official boundary, in Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, lies at about 230 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Merlot, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-milla.nerd_note: Kurtatsch's vineyards climb from about 220 m on the valley floor to over 900 m, so the village can grow Cabernet and Merlot at the bottom and Müller-Thurgau at the top within a few kilometres.

it-alto-adige-nafen.terroir: Quartz phyllite and moraine at roughly 650 to 950 m. The official boundary, in Funes/Villnöß, reaches from about 640 to 940 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Kerner.

it-alto-adige-penon.summary: Penon is a high hamlet above Kurtatsch, a cool site for Pinot Bianco, Pinot Grigio and Sauvignon; Kellerei Kurtatsch's top whites come from here.

it-alto-adige-punggl.terroir: Alluvial gravel. The official boundary, in Magrè/Margreid, reaches from about 210 to 500 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Merlot.

it-alto-adige-putznai.terroir: Gravel and moraine. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin and Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 220 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein, Cabernet.

it-alto-adige-rentsch.summary: Rentsch lies at the foot of the St. Magdalena hill on Bolzano's eastern edge, giving fragrant, cherry-scented Santa Maddalena and Lagrein. Several family estates of the classic zone have their farmhouses here.

it-alto-adige-ritten.summary: The Ritten UGA covers the vineyards on the lower slopes of the Ritten plateau, the mountain shelf north-east of Bolzano. At altitude the classic reds give way to Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero, crisp and aromatic.

it-alto-adige-rungg.terroir: Moraine and calcareous gravel. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin and Cortaccia/Kurtatsch, reaches from about 230 to 580 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-salurn-pfatten.terroir: Alluvial gravel of the Adige plain. The official boundary, in Salorno/Salurn, reaches from about 200 to 300 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio.

it-alto-adige-sauders.name: Sauders
it-alto-adige-sauders.summary: Sauders is a Villanders site reserved for Grüner Veltliner, a variety that has found a second home in the Eisacktal.
it-alto-adige-sauders.terroir: Quartz phyllite on steep slopes. The official boundary, in Villandro/Villanders, reaches from about 540 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Grüner Veltliner.
it-alto-adige-sauders.nerd_note: The Eisacktal is Alto Adige's white-wine valley, with steep terraces up to about 900 m and soils of quartz phyllite, granite and moraine; Cantina Valle Isarco in Klausen and the abbey of Neustift are its anchors.

it-alto-adige-siebeneich.summary: Siebeneich ('seven oaks') lies on the warm valley floor of Terlan towards Bolzano, a site for reds and whites: Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-siebeneich.terroir: Alluvial and porphyry debris. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan, reaches from about 240 to 500 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.

it-alto-adige-sirmian.summary: Sirmian lies above Nals on the way to Tisens, and is the source of Cantina Nals Margreid's Pinot Bianco Sirmian, one of Alto Adige's reference whites. The UGA allows Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay and Sauvignon.

it-alto-adige-soll.name: Söll
it-alto-adige-soll.summary: Söll is a hamlet on the slopes above Tramin and the heart of Alto Adige Gewürztraminer. Hofstätter's Kolbenhof and many of Cantina Tramin's top lots, including Nussbaumer, come from these warm, steep pergolas. The wines are intensely aromatic, with rose, lychee and spice, but surprisingly fresh.

it-alto-adige-st-anna.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-st-anna.summary: St. Anna lies on the Eppan slopes near the lakes, giving Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-st-anna.terroir: Morainic soils. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan, lies at about 410 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.

it-alto-adige-st-jacob.terroir: Steep limestone and dolomite debris facing south-east. The official boundary, in Termeno/Tramin, lies at about 360 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-st-josef.name: St. Josef
it-alto-adige-st-josef.summary: St. Josef am See lies on the shore of the Kalterer See (Lago di Caldaro), the warmest corner of the Überetsch, where Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot and Cabernet ripen easily. The lake gave its name to Kalterersee, once Austria-Hungary's favourite red; Manincor's estate stands here.
it-alto-adige-st-josef.terroir: Morainic gravel and lake sediments on slopes around the water, which stores heat. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 220 to 450 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Schiava, Lagrein, Merlot, Cabernet.

it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.summary: St. Nikolaus is a hamlet high above Kaltern, a cool site where Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero keep their freshness.
it-alto-adige-st-nikolaus.terroir: Calcareous debris from the Mendola range over moraine. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 390 to 840 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.

it-alto-adige-st-peter.terroir: Porphyry rock and morainic debris on south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, lies at about 330 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Sauvignon Blanc, Schiava, Lagrein.

it-alto-adige-steinacker.summary: Steinacker ('stone field') lies on the warm valley floor below Tramin, giving Chardonnay, Lagrein and Merlot.

it-alto-adige-terlano.name: Terlano
it-alto-adige-terlano.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon, Pinot Grigio, Riesling, Müller-Thurgau
it-alto-adige-terlano.summary: Terlano is the most famous white-wine village of Alto Adige, between Bolzano and Merano. Its cooperative, the Cantina Terlano (1893), holds back wines for 10 to 30 years before release, proving that Pinot Bianco and Sauvignon from porphyry soils can age like great Burgundy. Terlaner Classico comes from the steep porphyry slopes above the village.
it-alto-adige-terlano.terroir: Red quartz porphyry, sandy and mineral, on south-facing slopes up to about 900 m.
it-alto-adige-terlano.nerd_note: Cantina Terlano's 'Rarity' series releases wines that have spent more than a decade on fine lees in steel tanks.

it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.name: Alto Adige Terlano classico
it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.summary: The classico core of the Terlano subzone, covering the porphyry slopes of Terlan, Nals and Andrian, the historic home of Terlaner white blends, Pinot Bianco and Sauvignon renowned for their longevity.
it-alto-adige-terlano-classico.terroir: Quartz porphyry with sandy topsoil on steep south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan, Nalles/Nals and Andriano/Andrian, reaches from about 240 to 1780 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-tirol.name: Tirol
it-alto-adige-tirol.grapes: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero
it-alto-adige-tirol.summary: Tirol is the village above Meran that gave its name to the whole Tyrol through its castle, Schloss Tirol. Its UGA allows Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-tirol.terroir: Gneiss, mica schist and moraine on steep slopes. The official boundary, in Tirolo/Tirol, reaches from about 320 to 750 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-tirol.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-tirol.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.name: Unterfennberg-Hofstatt
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.summary: Unterfennberg-Hofstatt lies on the Fennberg, a mountain terrace at nearly 1,000 m above Margreid, and is reserved for Müller-Thurgau. Tiefenbrunner's Feldmarschall von Fenner, one of Italy's most famous Müller-Thurgaus, grows on this plateau.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.terroir: Limestone and dolomite on a high, cool terrace with large day-night temperature swings. The official boundary, in Magrè/Margreid, lies at about 970 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Müller-Thurgau.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.nerd_note: It is one of the highest vineyard UGAs of Alto Adige.
it-alto-adige-unterfennberg-hofstatt.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-val-venosta.name: Val Venosta
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.grapes: Riesling, Pinot Bianco, Pinot Nero, Müller-Thurgau, Kerner, Gewürztraminer
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.summary: The dry, high Vinschgau west of Merano, famous for apples, has a small number of vineyards at 500 to 900 m that make taut Riesling and Pinot Noir. Castel Juval, owned by the mountaineer Reinhold Messner, and Falkenstein (Franz Pratzner) are its best-known estates.
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.terroir: Gneiss and schist on the sunny northern side of a rain-shadow valley with very low rainfall.
it-alto-adige-val-venosta.nerd_note: Reinhold Messner, the first man to climb all 14 eight-thousanders, owns Castel Juval and its vineyard.

it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.name: Valle Isarco
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.grapes: Sylvaner, Kerner, Müller-Thurgau, Grüner Veltliner, Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Grigio, Zweigelt
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.summary: The Isarco (Eisack) valley north of Bolzano toward Bressanone and the Brenner Pass is Italy's northernmost wine zone, a land of steep terraces, monasteries and crisp, aromatic whites. Kerner, Sylvaner and Grüner Veltliner are specialities; Bressanone (Brixner) and Klausen are sub-areas. The Abbazia di Novacella (founded 1142) and the Cantina Valle Isarco co-op dominate, with growers like Kuenhof (Peter Pliger), Manni Nössing and Köfererhof.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.terroir: Schist, quartz-phyllite and glacial moraine at 500 to 900 m; cool, with strong day-night swings.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco.nerd_note: Kerner, a Schiava x Riesling cross bred in Württemberg in 1929, found its best home in Italy here.

it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.name: Alto Adige Valle Isarco Klausner Leitacher
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.summary: Klausner Leitacher is a traditional red-wine name within the Valle Isarco subzone, a Schiava-based red from the slopes around Klausen, the only red wine with its own name in this white-wine valley.
it-alto-adige-valle-isarco-klausner-leit.terroir: Quartz phyllite and moraine on the slopes around Klausen. The official boundary, in Chiusa/Klausen, Barbiano/Barbian, Velturno/Feldthurns and Villandro/Villanders, reaches from about 510 to 1060 m (terrain model).

it-alto-adige-vetzaner.name: Vetzaner
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.summary: Vetzan, near Schlanders, is the westernmost UGA of Alto Adige, at around 650 to 900 m in the upper Vinschgau. It gives taut Pinot Bianco, Riesling and Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist with sandy moraine, very dry and sunny. The official boundary, in Silandro/Schlanders, reaches from about 670 to 890 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Riesling, Pinot Nero.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.nerd_note: The Vinschgau is one of the driest valleys of the Alps, with under 500 mm of rain a year in places; growers once irrigated with the 'Waale', medieval channels cut along the slopes.
it-alto-adige-vetzaner.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-vorberg.name: Vorberg
it-alto-adige-vorberg.summary: Vorberg rises above Terlan towards Mölten and is the source of Cantina Terlano's Pinot Bianco Vorberg Riserva, a famously long-lived white. Terlan's whites are known for their ability to age decades, a quality the cooperative proves with its 'Rarity' releases.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.terroir: Quartz porphyry (Bozen volcanic rock) with sandy topsoil on steep south-facing slopes. The official boundary, in Terlano/Terlan and Meltina/Mölten, reaches from about 250 to 1030 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Pinot Bianco, Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.nerd_note: Terlano keeps old vintages on the lees in steel for ten years or more before release as 'Rarity'.
it-alto-adige-vorberg.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-alto-adige-wadleith.name: Wadleith
it-alto-adige-wadleith.grapes: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Cabernet
it-alto-adige-wadleith.summary: Wadleith lies on the warm slopes of Kaltern towards the lake, giving Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon, Lagrein and Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.terroir: Morainic gravel. The official boundary, in Caldaro/Kaltern, lies at about 290 m (terrain model). Varieties permitted under the UGA name: Chardonnay, Pinot Grigio, Sauvignon Blanc, Lagrein, Cabernet.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.nerd_note: UGA wines must come entirely from the named site, at yields at least 25 percent below the DOC maximum, with one to five permitted varieties per UGA, and must carry the Consorzio's UGA symbol on the label.
it-alto-adige-wadleith.classification: UGA (Unità Geografica Aggiuntiva) of Alto Adige / Südtirol DOC, one of 86 recognised by ministerial decree of 8 October 2024; first vintage 2024

it-chianti-classico-castellina.name: Castellina
it-chianti-classico-castellina.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-castellina.summary: One of the three founding members of the medieval Lega del Chianti, Castellina sits on the ridge that splits the Pesa and Elsa valleys. Its whole commune forms the UGA. The western side looks toward the Elsa and is warmer; soils mix alberese, sandstone and clay, and the wines tend to be broad-shouldered and dark-fruited, with Fonterutoli (Mazzei, in Chianti since 1435) as the historic name. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.name: Castelnuovo Berardenga
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-castelnuovo-berarden.summary: The southernmost and warmest UGA, where Chianti Classico runs down toward the clay hills of the Crete Senesi. Soils shift to Pliocene sands and marine clays with alberese, giving the zone's ripest, most generous Sangiovese with firm tannin. From 2027 its western part around Vagliagli becomes a separate UGA. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-gaiole.name: Gaiole
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-gaiole.summary: Gaiole spreads across the eastern Monti del Chianti, a high, wooded commune that includes Brolio, Coltibuono, Ama and Rietine. It was a founding Lega member and is home to some of the zone's highest vineyards (above 600 m at Lamole's neighbour ridges and around Montegrossi). Galestro and alberese give tense, mineral wines with long life. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-greve.name: Greve
it-chianti-classico-greve.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-greve.summary: The Greve UGA is the northern and eastern part of the commune once Panzano, and from 2027 Lamole and Montefioralle, are carved out. It is a large, varied area along the Greve valley with sandstone and galestro, and includes Ruffoli's high slopes (Querciabella) and Verrazzano, the family castle of the explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-lamole.name: Lamole
it-chianti-classico-lamole.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2027 vintage)
it-chianti-classico-lamole.summary: A tiny hamlet of terraces high above Greve (roughly 500 to 650 m), with dry-stone walls rebuilt by hand and sandstone soils (macigno) that give pale, high-toned, floral Sangiovese. Lamole becomes its own UGA from the 2027 vintage and is a poster child for altitude in a warming climate. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.name: Montefioralle
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2027 vintage)
it-chianti-classico-montefioralle.summary: A walled medieval village on the hill just west of Greve, believed to be the family home of Amerigo Vespucci. From 2027 it is the smallest of the new UGAs. Its slopes of galestro and alberese give fine, elegant wines. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-panzano.name: Panzano
it-chianti-classico-panzano.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-panzano.summary: Panzano is the frazione in the southwest of Greve commune famous for the Conca d'Oro, a south-facing amphitheatre of galestro and alberese that collects heat and gives some of the most complete Sangiovese in Tuscany. Its growers pioneered collective organic farming (the Unione Viticoltori di Panzano), and most of the slopes are organic. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-radda.name: Radda
it-chianti-classico-radda.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-radda.summary: Radda was the capital of the Lega del Chianti and is now the reference for high-altitude, galestro-driven Sangiovese: pale, perfumed and nervy, sometimes austere in youth. Vineyards sit at roughly 400 to 650 m. A group of growers, the Radda nel Bicchiere association, promoted the commune's identity long before UGAs existed. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.name: San Casciano
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-san-casciano.summary: The northern gateway to the zone, on lower, gentler hills toward Florence, with sandstone and Pliocene sands. Antinori's Tignanello vineyard and its Bargino winery sit in this area; the wines are often supple and aromatic. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.name: San Donato in Poggio
it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2023 rules)
it-chianti-classico-san-donato-in-poggio.summary: This UGA joins the western half of Barberino Tavarnelle with the northern tip of Poggibonsi, centred on the walled village of San Donato. It includes Isole e Olena and Monsanto, two estates that helped prove the area's class with sandstone and alberese slopes and cool evenings. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.name: Vagliagli
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.created: UGA of Chianti Classico (approved June 2021; effective 2027 vintage)
it-chianti-classico-vagliagli.summary: A hamlet in western Castelnuovo Berardenga, higher and cooler than the southern part of the commune, with alberese and sandstone. It becomes its own UGA from the 2027 vintage; producers there may choose the new name or the old one once. For now the UGA name may appear only on Chianti Classico Gran Selezione.

it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.name: Lago di Caldaro classico
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.summary: The classico heartland of Lago di Caldaro (Kalterersee), the light, cherry-scented Schiava that was once the everyday red of the Habsburg empire. The classico zone surrounds the lake and the villages of Kaltern and Eppan; a 'scelto' or 'Auslese' version must reach higher ripeness.
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.terroir: Morainic gravel and limestone debris around the lake, warm and sheltered. The official boundary, in Appiano/Eppan and Caldaro/Kaltern, reaches from about 210 to 810 m (terrain model).
it-lago-di-caldaro-classico.nerd_note: Schiava (Vernatsch) covered most of Alto Adige's vineyards until the 1980s; it now covers under a tenth.

it-santa-maddalena.name: Santa Maddalena
it-santa-maddalena.summary: The hillside vineyards around the little church of St. Magdalena on the north-eastern edge of Bolzano make Alto Adige's classic Schiava: pale ruby, fragrant with violets, almond and cherry, a touch of Lagrein for colour. Local lore holds that in the 1930s it was ranked among Italy's three great reds, alongside Barolo and Barbaresco. The Classico core is on the steep slopes of Rencio and St. Magdalena.
it-santa-maddalena.terroir: Morainic and porphyry slopes rising behind Bolzano, very warm and sunny.
it-santa-maddalena.nerd_note: The UGAs inside the classico area include St. Justina, Leitach, Rentsch and Prazöll, all small hillside hamlets of Bolzano.

it-santa-maddalena-classico.name: Santa Maddalena classico
it-santa-maddalena-classico.summary: The classico zone of Santa Maddalena (St. Magdalener), the steep hill north-east of Bolzano around the little church of St. Magdalena. Its Schiava-based reds, often with up to 15 percent Lagrein, are the most structured expression of the grape, with cherry, almond and violet.
it-santa-maddalena-classico.terroir: Morainic sands and gravel over quartz porphyry on very steep, south-facing pergola slopes. The official boundary, in Bolzano/Bozen, reaches from about 270 to 860 m (terrain model).
it-santa-maddalena-classico.nerd_note: In the 1930s Mussolini's government is said to have ranked Santa Maddalena among Italy's three great wines with Barolo and Barbaresco.
